configuration_loc.conclusion: Both include deployment, CI and governance configuration, but service topology and lock-file formats differ.

deployment_footprint.conclusion: Framework consolidates the app/UI image but isolates more Temporal task queues; custom separates more application services and adds Redis.

deterministic_scenario_latency.conclusion: The executions share a host but not fixtures, interpreter, sample count or profile boundaries. Values are retained as reproducibility evidence and must not be ranked.

custom.samples: 3 per local profile after one warmup

framework.samples: 20 per local profile, except ledger replay with 50

direct_dependencies.conclusion: Framework Aegis adds orchestration and UI framework dependencies while custom Aegis owns more mechanics directly.

documentation_loc.conclusion: Physical documentation volume is disclosed; navigability and claim accuracy matter more than size.

evaluation_coverage.conclusion: Custom has a broader case catalog. Framework reuses fewer real cross-layer cases and does not manufacture count parity.

failure_semantics.conclusion: Both are at-least-once across external effects and require idempotency or explicit ambiguity/reconciliation; framework histories never establish enterprise authority.
failure_semantics.custom: Application events plus PostgreSQL/Redis workers own delivery, lease, retry and reconciliation mechanics directly.
failure_semantics.framework: Temporal owns durable scheduling/retry and LangGraph owns bounded cognitive checkpoints; application events, intent, approval, fencing, receipts and reconciliation remain truth.

implementation_effort_proxy.conclusion: Changed-file and line counts are a reproducible size proxy only; neither repository records comparable person-hours.

learning_curve.conclusion: Framework Aegis accelerates conventional framework literacy but increases breadth; custom Aegis concentrates complexity in code the team fully owns.
learning_curve.custom: Requires deeper study of bespoke ledger, worker, lease, retry and reconciliation code with fewer orchestration-framework concepts.
learning_curve.framework: Requires application authority design plus LangGraph, Temporal, Langfuse/OTel, FastAPI/Pydantic, pgvector, React/TanStack/Zod, protocol SDKs and infrastructure tooling.

locked_dependencies.conclusion: Python closure is materially larger for framework Aegis. npm package and pnpm entry counts are not structurally identical.

operational_burden.conclusion: Temporal removes custom queue/timer/replay mechanics but adds managed service, payload, retention, versioning, cost and failover operations.
operational_burden.custom: Operate PostgreSQL, Redis transport/leases/reconcilers, custom worker semantics, Kubernetes, identity, telemetry and signed supply chain.
operational_burden.framework: Operate PostgreSQL, Temporal namespace/queues/history/versioning, Kubernetes, identity, telemetry, signed supply chain and framework upgrades.

portability_and_lock_in.conclusion: Neither design is lock-in free. Accept only if ledger export, projection rebuild and replacement rehearsal preserve identical application truth.
portability_and_lock_in.custom: Fewer orchestration-framework formats, but custom Redis/worker/event contracts and bespoke operational tooling must be maintained or migrated.
portability_and_lock_in.framework: Provider-neutral ports and application-ledger rebuild reduce coupling, but Temporal histories, LangGraph checkpoint formats and a larger SDK closure add migration work.

production_loc.conclusion: The custom implementation contains more product-source LOC under the shared physical-line scope; LOC alone does not establish quality or ownership burden.

security_controls.conclusion: Control families overlap, but no independent penetration, live identity, sandbox, partner, managed recovery or certification evidence exists for either.
security_controls.custom: Equivalent application-owned control families with custom scheduling/worker enforcement and its own release-readiness/risk manifests.
security_controls.framework: Deny-default identity/policy, forced RLS, budgets, citation gates, exact approvals, fencing, telemetry minimization, sandbox/protocol boundaries and signed supply chain.

services.conclusion: Framework Aegis replaces custom Redis worker transport with Temporal but carries a managed workflow control-plane dependency.

test_loc.conclusion: Both repositories invest heavily in executable tests; coverage denominators and omitted environment adapters differ.

framework.comparison_scope: Layer 16 working tree measured against the exact Layer 15 base

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: The bounded cognitive topology removes more scheduling code than its checkpoint/migration burden.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: Generic bounded fan-out/fan-in, reducer, conditional routing and checkpoint scheduling.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Rebuild artifacts/read models from application facts; replace OrchestratorPort and discard checkpoints.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Checkpoint serialization drift, topology replay incompatibility and accidental framework-state authority.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Roles, capabilities, evidence projection, citations, budgets, policy, approval, audit, effects and deterministic application artifacts.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: Checkpoint storage, compatibility, pruning, recursion bounds and graph-version migrations.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: The graph needs dynamic authority, opaque replay-only state or cannot be rebuilt from application facts.
framework_verdicts.verdict: Adopt only as a bounded non-authoritative cognitive adapter.

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: Long waits and cross-process recovery justify a dedicated durable workflow service.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: Queue leases, heartbeats, timers, signals, activity retry, worker recovery and workflow replay mechanics.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Keep opaque workflow references and application outbox/events; drain/reconcile and reissue stable operations to a replacement scheduler.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Nondeterministic workflow changes, history retention/loss, retry duplication, saturation and managed-service coupling.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Transactional outbox, current authorization, budgets, intent, idempotency, approval truth, fencing, receipts, reconciliation and audit.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: Namespace, task queues, payload codec, identity, retention, versioning, capacity, cost, failover and history export.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: A simple database worker suffices or history/export/privacy/cost constraints are unacceptable.
framework_verdicts.verdict: Adopt for durable orchestration, never as application truth.

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: Sanitized count/digest UX adds debugging value under reviewed retention.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: Optional trace and evaluation experiment UX.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Keep OTLP semantics and local deterministic reports; delete Langfuse data without losing truth.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Telemetry outage, schema/client drift and accidental payload capture.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Application audit, replay, authorization, SLO semantics, redaction policy or local release gates.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: Backend, retention, access control, sampling, exporter monitoring and privacy review.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: Automatic graph capture or hosted data policy conflicts with privacy boundaries.
framework_verdicts.verdict: Optional manual adapter only; automatic tracing stays disabled.

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: Typed HTTP/OpenAPI delivery fits the service and strict models remain explicit.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: HTTP routing, OpenAPI mechanics, parsing and strict runtime validation boilerplate.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Preserve strict domain contracts and delivery ports; replace the ASGI adapter.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Validation/coercion changes, generated-schema drift and middleware ordering mistakes.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Identity establishment, authorization, anti-enumeration, idempotency, tenant scoping or domain invariants.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: ASGI lifecycle, dependency/security updates, schema compatibility and validation-performance review.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: Framework dependency injection obscures authority or coercive schemas weaken boundaries.
framework_verdicts.verdict: Adopt at delivery and contract boundaries, not for enterprise policy.

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: The SDK is official, exact-pinned, retry-disabled and isolated behind a narrow port.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: Wire protocols, authentication plumbing, object encoding/decoding and provider-specific request mechanics.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Keep provider-neutral ports and deterministic fakes; replace one vendor adapter at a time.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Default retries, changed models, transport behavior, new fields and supply-chain findings.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Tenant policy, SSRF/egress controls, secret references, quotas, retries, provenance, citations, target binding or reconciliation.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: Large transitive dependency trees, provider release cadence and compatibility testing.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: It widens authority, hides network behavior or cannot meet pinning/privacy requirements.
framework_verdicts.verdict: Prefer official mechanics behind application-owned controls.

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: PostgreSQL locality and workload scale are acceptable and rebuild is rehearsed.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: Separate vector database service and custom vector storage/index protocol.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Rebuild the derived index from application records/facts plus retained approved content; keep neutral retrieval contracts.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Recall/latency drift, extension compatibility and treating derived similarity as authority.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Memory acceptance, provenance, ACL/classification filters, retention, legal hold, MMR/context policy, citations or erasure.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: Extension lifecycle, ANN index tuning, vacuum/storage growth, backups and query-plan qualification.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: Scale, isolation or managed extension constraints require a dedicated engine.
framework_verdicts.verdict: Adopt as a disposable derived index, never memory truth.

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: The operator workflow benefits from typed rich-client state under a same-origin BFF.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: Rendering, routing, query/cache/table mechanics and client runtime parsing.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Retain backend contracts and server-owned decisions; replace the UI without changing authority.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Cache bleed, schema drift, XSS regressions and rapid ecosystem upgrades.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Server authorization, tenant cache teardown policy, approval semantics, CSRF/origin, redaction or audit.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: Node toolchain, browser matrix, bundle, dependency audits and accessibility testing.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: A static/server-rendered interface meets needs with materially less attack and upgrade surface.
framework_verdicts.verdict: Adopt for derived operator UX; all mutations remain server-authorized.

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: A reviewed partner needs interoperable read/proposal workflows with exact trust pins.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: Current protocol wire types, negotiation, transport, card and route mechanics.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Keep neutral application task/artifact contracts; disable a peer or replace its adapter.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Schema/card drift, confused deputy, replay, denial of wallet and untrusted content escalation.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Workload identity, peer trust, tenant purpose/RBAC, quotas, SSRF, provenance, citations, approval or effects.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: Spec/SDK cadence, partner conformance, PKI/token brokerage, egress and revocation operations.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: The peer requires direct effects, self-asserted tenancy or uncontrolled federation.
framework_verdicts.verdict: Adopt only as an untrusted proposal/read adapter.

framework_verdicts.adopt_when: The organization can operate the control planes and enforce reviewed immutable promotion.
framework_verdicts.code_removed: Kubernetes rollout primitives, Terraform dependency/state mechanics, GitHub build orchestration and Sigstore verification plumbing.
framework_verdicts.exit_strategy: Use OCI digests, Kustomize, SQL, OTLP and provider-neutral application ports; export state and rehearse replacement.
framework_verdicts.failure_and_upgrade_risks: Mutable inputs, state drift, controller/API changes, credential scope and supply-chain compromise.
framework_verdicts.not_replaced: Release approval, branch governance, application fencing, restore acceptance, SLO policy or compliance evidence.
framework_verdicts.operational_cost: Clusters, cloud state, controllers, action pinning, registry/signing, drift, upgrades and on-call.
framework_verdicts.reject_when: The deployment footprint exceeds team capability or required live controls cannot be owned.
framework_verdicts.verdict: The checked-in reference is locally qualified; live infrastructure remains a hard gate.

measurement_method.dependencies: Direct runtime dependencies come from project dependencies and UI dependencies. Locked Python packages come from uv.lock or the pinned custom requirements.lock; UI lock entry counts are disclosed separately because npm and pnpm lock structures differ.
measurement_method.effort_proxy: One-commit changed-file/addition/deletion counts only. They are not person-hours, complexity, quality or maintainability measures.
measurement_method.latency: Both pinned revisions were executed on the same Apple arm64 host on 2026-08-18 with Python 3.14.7 for framework and Python 3.13.15 for custom. Framework uses 20 or 50 samples; custom uses three. Fixtures and profile boundaries differ, so results are regression evidence only and no cross-repository latency ranking is supported.
measurement_method.loc: Physical lines including comments and blanks. Production is Python under src plus non-test TypeScript/TSX under the operator UI source. Tests are Python tests plus UI unit/e2e test sources. Configuration includes workflows, deployment, eval, migration, observability, qualification and package/build configuration but excludes dependency lock files. Documentation is every tracked Markdown file.
